big_picture_notes: 2 Corinthians is an emotionally charged apologia where Paul defends integrity and apostolic authority while seeking reconciliation. The letter coheres through the paradox that divine power is displayed in human weakness (1:3–11; 4:7–12; 12:7–10). Macro‑movement: A) Reconciliation and New‑Covenant ministry (1–7), B) The Jerusalem collection (8–9), C) Polemical defense against the ‘super‑apostles’ (10–13). Literary glue: repeated paraklēsis (comfort/encouragement), boasting redefined as boasting in weakness, peristasis catalogs, and Spirit/new‑covenant contrasts (letter vs Spirit).

stories.story_title: Reconciliation and the Ministry of the New Covenant
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Start (1:1) epistolary opening and blessing of comfort; end (7:16) resolves anxiety with joy and confidence, closing the reconciliation arc. Glue: comfort/encouragement repetition, weakness→power paradox, and developing defense of new‑covenant ministry (chs. 3–5).

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Paul and Timothy greet the church in Corinth and all the saints in Achaia.
Blessing the Father of compassion who comforts us in affliction so we can comfort others.
Asian affliction near‑death; deliverance elicits prayers and thanksgiving. Devices: narrative disclosure, purpose result (‘so that thanks may be given’).

scenes.scene_name: Our Boast: Sincerity, Not Worldly Wisdom
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A clear conscience of holy, sincere conduct, that they may boast of one another in the day of the Lord.
The intended double-visit, and Paul's denial that he plans by fickle human 'yes and no.'

scenes.scene_name: In Christ It Is Always Yes
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's faithfulness: every promise is 'Yes' in Christ, to whom we say 'Amen' to God's glory.

scenes.scene_name: Spirit as Seal and Pastoral Pain
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God establishes, anoints, seals; delayed visit to spare sorrow; love motive. Devices: covenant seal/arrabōn, pastoral rationale.
The majority's punishment is enough; now reaffirm love lest he be overwhelmed by sorrow.
Paul forgives in Christ's presence so that Satan, whose schemes are known, gains no advantage.
Troas narrative turns to triumph metaphor; not peddlers but commissioned. Devices: aroma of life/death, anti‑mercenary contrast.

scenes.scene_name: Letter and Spirit; Sufficiency from God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Corinthians as letter; ministers of new covenant—letter kills, Spirit gives life. Devices: commendation question, letter/Spirit contrast.

scenes.scene_name: The Greater Glory of the New Ministry
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: If the fading ministry of death came with glory, how much more the enduring ministry of the Spirit.
Unlike veiled Moses, we are bold; yet a veil remains over hearts at the reading of the old covenant.
Turning to the Lord lifts the veil; with unveiled faces we are transformed from glory to glory.
Renounce underhanded ways; God shines light (Gen 1:3) in hearts. Devices: negative self‑definition, creation allusion.
The surpassing power is God's, not ours — hard pressed but not crushed, struck down but not destroyed.
Always bearing Jesus' death so His life is revealed; death at work in us, life in you.

scenes.scene_name: Faith That Speaks; Raised with Jesus
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The same spirit of faith believes and speaks, sure the One who raised Jesus will raise us too.
Outer decay/inner renewal; earthly tent vs heavenly building; Spirit as guarantee. Devices: contrast sets, eschatological metaphor, arrabōn.

scenes.scene_name: We Walk by Faith; the Judgment Seat
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Confident though absent from the Lord, aspiring to please Him, for all must appear before His judgment seat.
Knowing the fear of the Lord, Paul persuades men, giving the Corinthians cause to boast in the heart.
One died for all, so all died; anyone in Christ is a new creation — the old has passed away.
God reconciles through Christ; implore: be reconciled; ‘now is the day of salvation’. Devices: embassy appeal, prophetic citation (Isa 49:8).

scenes.scene_name: Commended as Servants of God in Endurance
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: No obstacle placed, but commendation through great endurance, purity, and the weapons of righteousness.
The paradoxes of true ministry: sorrowful yet rejoicing, poor yet making many rich, having nothing yet all.
Paul's heart open wide to the Corinthians, asking them in fair exchange to open theirs.
Imperative separation; five rhetorical questions; cleanse in holiness. Devices: incompatibility contrasts, promise‑based exhortation.
Paul has wronged no one; his confidence and pride in them overflow with joy in all troubles.

scenes.scene_name: Comforted by the Coming of Titus
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Restless in Macedonia, God comforted the downcast by Titus's arrival and the Corinthians' longing.
No regret for the sorrowful letter, for godly sorrow leads to repentance and salvation, not death.
The earnestness and zeal it bred, proving them innocent — and refreshing the spirit of Titus.
Paul's boasting to Titus was vindicated, and his complete confidence in them restored.

stories.story_title: The Collection for the Jerusalem Saints
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Start (8:1) shifts to the grace of giving; end (9:15) doxology to God’s indescribable gift. Glue: grace/giving/service vocabulary, exemplum of Macedonians, Christological poverty‑riches principle, sowing/reaping metaphor.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: In deep poverty their abundant joy overflowed in rich generosity, giving themselves first to the Lord.

scenes.scene_name: Excel in This Grace of Giving
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: As Titus began, so let the Corinthians, excelling in everything, also excel in the grace of giving.

scenes.scene_name: Christ Became Poor; Finish the Work
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Testing love by Christ's example, who became poor to make us rich — now complete what you began.

scenes.scene_name: Equality: Your Surplus Meets Their Need
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The acceptable gift is according to what one has; present surplus meeting need, that there be equality.
Titus comes eagerly, with the brother praised by all the churches, chosen to carry the offering.

scenes.scene_name: Avoiding Criticism; Proof of Your Love
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Care taken to be honorable before God and men; show these messengers the proof of your love.
Superfluous to write yet necessary; ensure generosity, not grudging. Devices: gentle pressure, preparation logistics.
Sow bountifully; God loves cheerful giver; supplier multiplies seed. Devices: agricultural metaphor, aphorisms, provision promise.
Service supplies needs, produces thanksgiving, proves obedience; doxology. Devices: threefold outcome, climactic thanksgiving.

stories.story_title: Paul’s Defense of His Apostolic Authority
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Start (10:1) abrupt tonal shift to direct polemic; end (13:14) trinitarian benediction. Glue: boasting redefined, weakness/power antithesis, legal ‘two or three witnesses’ framing for impending visit.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Paul appeals in Christ's gentleness; we do not war by the flesh, but with weapons of divine power.
Demolishing arguments and taking every thought captive to obey Christ; belonging to Christ alike.

scenes.scene_name: Authority for Building Up, Not Tearing Down
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Not ashamed of his authority; what he is in letters when absent he will be in deed when present.
Refusing to compare himself with the self-commenders, boasting only within God's assigned field.

scenes.scene_name: Let Him Who Boasts Boast in the Lord
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Hope to preach beyond them as faith grows — for the approved is the one the Lord commends.
Bear with ‘foolishness’; betrothal metaphor; not inferior to ‘super‑apostles’. Devices: paternal imagery, serpent deception warning.
Paul humbled himself, taking no support but from other churches — not because he does not love them.
Undercutting the boasters: false apostles, like Satan as an angel of light, will meet their deserved end.

scenes.scene_name: Bear with Me as a Fool
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Paul asks to be received as a fool that he too may boast a little, as many boast in the flesh.
The wise Corinthians endure those who enslave and exploit them — to his shame, he was 'too weak.'

scenes.scene_name: Are They Servants of Christ? Far More
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Hebrew, Israelite, Abraham's seed — yet far more in labors, imprisonments, beatings, lashes, and stoning.
Perils on every road and sea, hunger and cold, and the daily pressure of concern for all the churches.
Burning for the weak and the fallen; if he must boast, he boasts of his weakness before God.
Lowered in a basket through a window to escape the governor under King Aretas.

scenes.scene_name: Caught Up to the Third Heaven
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Visions and revelations: a man caught up to Paradise, hearing inexpressible things.
Boasting only in weakness; a thorn, a messenger of Satan, given to keep him from conceit.

scenes.scene_name: My Grace Is Sufficient for You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Three times he pleaded; the Lord's grace is enough, for power is perfected in weakness.

scenes.scene_name: The Signs of a True Apostle
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Driven to foolish boasting; signs, wonders, and miracles marked him, though he was no burden to them.

scenes.scene_name: Coming a Third Time, Not a Burden
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Seeking not their possessions but them, gladly spending himself for their souls.

scenes.scene_name: Did I Exploit You Through Anyone?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Refuting the charge of craftiness: neither Titus nor the brother took advantage of them.

scenes.scene_name: Final Warnings and Coming in Power
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: For building up; two or three witnesses; weakness/power pattern in Christ and in us. Devices: legal framing, Christological analogy.
Examine yourselves; Paul’s aim is not severity but building up. Devices: imperative focus shift, purpose statement.
Final imperatives for peace; holy kiss; grace–love–fellowship benediction. Devices: closing formulae, trinitarian blessing.
